name: google_search_chromium
description: WALLED ON THIS ENGINE as of 2026-09-18 (research/google_reopened_2026_09_18.json): chromium is refused on Google -- 3 of 3 on the same url, settings and egress where the camoufox twin passed 11 of 11, and 0 of its own 6 runs through the pool in the 09-17 sweep (all four Google presets together were 1 of 24 there, and that single pass was google_shopping_camoufox/us -- the camoufox side). Use google_search_camoufox, which carries the data. The measurement crossed the engines on ONE egress, this host's own address, which is what makes 11 of 11 against 0 of 3 mean anything. This twin nevertheless stays on the residential pool (`prem_res_rotating`) while its camoufox sibling leaves directly: a call to a twin measured refused must spend a pool exit, never the host address the camoufox twin depends on (review on #136, 2026-09-22). This is the reverse of the 2026-09-02 verdict (camoufox walled 24/24, stealth-off chromium through), so re-measure rather than trusting either line for long. It keeps the pool's rotate-on-block recovery (tests/presets/test_google_search_interstitial.py); only its camoufox twin, on the direct path, is single-attempt. The locales here also build www.google.com now: every country ccTLD is refused outright, including one coherent with its own exit. UPDATE 2026-09-05: timeout_ms 45000 -> 34000 (per-phase; see test_builtin_timeout_fits_the_first_attempt). The 45000 figures below are the 2026-08-28 state. Google web search (organic results). Returns one flat array per field across organic results; consumers zip them by index. ROW-ALIGNMENT INVARIANT: every field must match exactly one node per result, so all four scope to #rso div.tF2Cxc — the organic-result container Google renders for EVERY result (div.g was retired) — which also keeps ads/PAA/nav blocks out. `snippets` anchors to div.tF2Cxc itself (not to div[data-sncf='1'], which exists ONLY when the result has a snippet) and digs the text out of that container's html by regex: a snippet-less result then yields null in its own slot instead of shrinking the array and silently shifting every later row up one. Never point a field at an element that only exists when its value does. UPDATE 2026-09-04 -- `links` ARE FOLLOWABLE AGAIN, and `display_urls` is added. Google confirmed on 2026-08-26 that it rewrites every result href to an opaque `/goto?url=` token; the token cannot be decoded, and the CALLER WARNING below describes that RAW href. This preset now (1) reads `display_urls` -- the display URL Google still prints under every title, `<cite>https://www.wired.com › story</cite>` -- from the organic container's html with the same regex + strip_tags recipe `snippets` uses, so a container with no cite yields null IN ITS OWN SLOT rather than shortening the column (each container repeats the cite in a sibling block; the regex takes the first; in the 2026-08-28 capture it sits INSIDE the same `<a>` as the `<h3>`, 8 of 8); and (2) sets `resolve_redirects: ["links"]`, so the worker resolves each stub to its destination after parsing -- the mechanism, its bounds and what it refuses are documented on `ScrapeRequest.resolve_redirects`. Live after deploy: every stub resolved on every run that reached a SERP (research/goto_v2_google_search_chromium.json). WHAT THE WRAPPER MEANS: a source that tested both reports Google serves `/goto` stubs only to sessions it has classified as automated and plain hrefs to ordinary browsing, so the presence of stubs is itself a verdict on the session -- a softer one than /sorry; asset blocking off, `humanize` and an 8 s warmup dwell did not change it (research/google_probe_2026_09_04_direct_links_probe.json). CALLER WARNING (raw href) -- `links` as read from the page ARE NOT FOLLOWABLE DESTINATIONS: every organic href Google serves here is a RELATIVE redirect stub of the form /goto?url=CAES... , not a URL. Nothing recovers the target from it -- the payload is opaque bytes, so no selector change, `urljoin` or `base64_decode` helps. Recorded by an earlier audit, unjudgeable on 2026-08-27 (zero rows on both twins, so no links to inspect), and REPRODUCED on 2026-08-28 once the wait fix below recovered real SERPs: all 23 links across the three google_search_chromium runs that returned rows are /goto?url= stubs (de#0 8/8, de#1 8/8, uk#1 7/7, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json), pinned by tests/presets/test_google_search_interstitial.py::TestRealSerpMarkupStillMatches::test_links_are_the_real_goto_redirect_stubs. `titles` and `snippets` are usable; treat `links` as a row marker, not a destination. This was an open defect until 2026-09-04; it is identical on both engine twins, and both twins now carry the same resolution. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-18: this preset used to route to the locale's country domain (google.de, google.co.uk, ...) and to take its exit from `proxy_country`. The first is gone -- every locale builds www.google.com (ccTLDs are refused outright); the second stays for this twin, which exits through the pool. `proxy_country: GB` on `us` routes this twin's pool exit through GB while the market stays US (gl=us): Google blocked the pool's US range hardest (TestGoogleBuiltinPresetsExitViaGB). Materializer must lowercase `country` for gl= and derive a language code for hl= from the locale. ENGINE: Chromium (Playwright), stealth off. chromium_webgl_identity()'s host-aligned WebGL claim (an AMD Radeon 780M string under a Windows UA) does NOT apply here: it runs only inside stealth_config(), which src/browser/runner.py:194 reaches only when stealth is on, so this preset ships the browser's raw headless WebGL identity instead. No fingerprint_profile, which the Chromium runner would accept and ignore. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): THIS PRESET RETURNED NO DATA ON EITHER VARIANT — 0/6 runs each, and they fail for different reasons. This variant never reached a SERP: 6/6 runs ended on google.com/sorry/index with all three retries spent and the block heuristic fired (HTTP 429, or /sorry served as a 200) — an ACCESS problem, unrelated to the wait strategy below, that this task does not fix. google_search_camoufox ended on the requested …/search?q=… URL on 6/6 with HTTP 200 and no block, and still extracted nothing (0 rows, "field 'titles': required selector not found"). ROOT CAUSE SETTLED 2026-08-28 (task 5, by capture, on the Camoufox twin — this variant cannot reach the page to confirm the same shell, but shares this preset's parsing recipe and wait strategy so the fix ships on both): `wait_until: domcontentloaded` returns before the redirect completes — Google serves a JS bounce shell at this stage (91,619 bytes live 2026-08-28/DE; 82 characters of visible body text after stripping script/style — "Klicke hier, wenn du nach einigen Sekunden nicht automatisch weitergeleitet wirst", i.e. "click here if you aren't redirected automatically after a few seconds"; zero #rso, zero h3, zero div.tF2Cxc, zero /goto?url=), not a captcha, not /sorry, not a consent wall. Measured live 2026-08-28 (Camoufox): a single fetch with `wait_until: load` (no selector) leaves the shell and resolves the redirect for real — landing on either the SERP or google.com/sorry depending on whether the exit passes Google's JS check — where `domcontentloaded` never observes either outcome, only ever the shell. Fixed the same way `yandex_search` was (read that preset first): `wait_until: load` plus `wait_for_selector: #rso`. This splits into two distinct, correctly-classified outcomes instead of one silent success: if the redirect leaves the page stuck on this shell (URL unchanged, not a recognised block endpoint), `wait_for_selector` genuinely times out and raises `selector_not_found: #rso`, which `is_selector_miss()` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:132) treats as retry-worthy; if instead it lands on `google.com/sorry`, `redirected_to_block()` (src/browser/runner.py:1095, mirrored at src/browser/camoufox_runner.py:441) recognises the URL BEFORE `wait_for_selector` is ever called, skips the wait entirely (no extra latency over the old config), and the block classifier sets `blocked=True` with `"Captcha/block detected by heuristic"` — rotation then happens on `fetch_result.blocked` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:646), not on a selector miss. Either way the old domcontentloaded-only config's single silent "0 rows, no error" stop is gone. `timeout_ms` raised 30000->45000 to match the 3-phase (warmup+goto+selector) budget yandex_search already uses; at PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s this fits on the fast-fail path (attempt 1 affordable ≈37.5s of the 45s requested, shortened-and-logged exactly like yandex's own attempt 1) but costs a real attempt: in the pathological case where every phase burns its full timeout, 3 phases afford only ONE full attempt before the 120s ceiling is spent (attempt 2 reported "not started"), where the old 2-phase/30000ms config could still afford two. A genuinely blocked run is not slower, though — see redirected_to_block above; only a run that stays ambiguously stuck (not yet recognised as a block) pays the extra phase's time. This changed `/api/v1/search?engine=google`'s latency too, while that endpoint pinned this preset by name (it now routes to google_search_camoufox, which shares this wait strategy): it materialized it with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override (`_proxy_override`/`_engine_override` only ever set proxy/engine fields), so a caller there waited up to ~37.5s longer for a real answer on a clean exit, or the same block-speed dead end on a burned one. This variant's own access block is UNCHANGED and NOT fixed by this task: its audit figure is 6/6 at /sorry for THIS preset alone (12/12 was this preset + google_shopping_chromium COMBINED, not one preset's number) — not re-tested live in this round because a prior live check already reached a real SERP once (n=1, see google_search_camoufox's description note on exit-reputation variance) and this task was told not to spend further live Google traffic verifying it. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 3/6 runs returned a REAL SERP -- de 8 rows twice, uk 7 rows once -- against 0/6 on 08-27, when all six ended at /sorry. The remaining 3 (uk#0, us#0, us#1) still end on google.com/sorry with the block heuristic fired and 3 retries spent: that is the ACCESS problem this branch never claimed to fix, and it is reported as a block, not as a wait-strategy failure. The wait strategy itself is confirmed by what is now ABSENT: not one run in the 08-28 record stops on the interstitial shell, i.e. there is no longer any google run that returns HTTP 200 with 0 rows and no block flag -- the exact silent stop the old domcontentloaded config produced 6/6 on the Camoufox twin one day earlier. Recovering real SERPs where 08-27 had none also confirms the prediction that `load` + #rso resolves the redirect instead of observing only the shell. n=2 per locale: the 3/6 access rate is this day's exit reputation, not a stable figure. CALLER TIMEOUT, CONFIRMED: one attempt of this preset now costs ~36s -- every google run in the 08-28 record carries "attempt 1/3 shortened to ~36000ms of the requested 45000ms to fit the page-task ceiling" (measured 35.7-36.4s) -- and a job that spends all three attempts reached took_ms 59058 (google_search_chromium/us) and 57193 (google_search_camoufox/us), before any queue wait. `/api/v1/search?engine=google` answers from google_search_camoufox as its JS-SERP route (src/api/search.py, ENGINES) with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override, so it inherits that twin's numbers verbatim, and yozh-law-checker's backend/app/services/scraper_search_client.py calls /api/v1/search with `timeout=60` and has four `return None` degrade paths. THAT CLIENT IS NOT AFFECTED TODAY: it calls the endpoint only with engine="yandex", which routes to yandex_search_camoufox and is untouched by this change. The consequence is conditional on that client switching to engine="google", at which point a blocked or retrying Google job legitimately outlives its 60s budget and the caller receives None with nothing to log, indistinguishable from an empty SERP. OPERATOR ACTION, IF AND WHEN THAT SWITCH HAPPENS: raise that client's timeout to at least 90s (clear of the 59.1s worst job measured here, still under PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s), or -- if 60s is a hard product constraint -- log the timeout degrade distinctly so "we gave up waiting" is never reported as "Google returned nothing".
